pr_title: Improve IndexOf handling in regex source generator / compiler
pr_body:
This PR does a few related things:
1. Consolidates _most_ (but not all) use of IndexOf variants into a single helper that can then be used from multiple locations to avoid code duplication and make it easier for us to extend in the future with additional IndexOf variants.
2. Stops using IndexOf when doing lazy backtracking in an optional.
3. Special-cases "any" repeaters to not do any character checking.
4. Adds use of IndexOf (via the new helper) into repeaters.

Fixes #77905 (mostly)

issue_context.title: Consolidate IndexOf variations into helper in regex source generator and compiler
issue_context.body: The regex source generator and compiler have grown to emit more and more IndexOf variations and to do so in more and more places. Each time we add a new variation, we're having to find and augment multiple locations in the generator, and each time we identify a new vectorization opportunity, we have to be able to emit use of all of those variations. We need to consolidate most if not all of these into a single helper that can be used from multiple locations to emit the right IndexOf calls. Then when we add additional IndexOf-like support, we can do so in a single place and have it accrue value to all uses where the calls are emitted.

review_comments: Judging from the old code, we actually weren't emitting the timeout check here, right?
Correct.  We used to, and then we removed that as part of overhauling how/where we emit timeout checks... the comment was just stale.

I know it precedes this PR, but should we be guarding against `5` if we're not using `IndexOfAny`? The rest of the `*Any*` helpers are vectorized up to 4.

`4` has a similar story where MONO doesn't have a vectorized path. Once #68328 is available, should we defer such cases to _it_, as it can make the optimal runtime decision?

> I know it precedes this PR, but should we be guarding against 5 if we're not using IndexOfAny? The rest of the *Any* helpers are vectorized up to 4.

It's not 100% correct, but it's also a reasonable limit that prevents the code complexity from getting out of hand.

> Once https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/68328 is available, should we defer such cases to it, as it can make the optimal runtime decision?

I'm very hesitant to do that.  The source generator can generate very efficient loops and set tests at compile time.  I expect it would end up being a deoptimization, both in startup time and in throughput, to always delegate to IndexOfAny.

> to always delegate to IndexOfAny

By always, do you mean for all sets of 4 & 5 characters?

I mean for anything we're not sure it's going to optimize / vectorize.  What if those 4 or 5 characters aren't ASCII?  Will the probabilistic map be employed / precomputed?  Will it necessarily be better?  And if so, would it not be better for the source generator to precompute that?  I've reluctantly accepted that for some things it makes sense to pay the startup overhead of the IndexOfAnyValues stuff, but I don't want to start pushing more and more out of the source generation across that tradeoff.

> What if those 4 or 5 characters aren't ASCII? Will the probabilistic map be employed / precomputed?

Depends on how many specialized cases we wanted to implement, but judging by my current local implementation it would mean using the 4 value vectorized helper when not on Mono, otherwise deferring to a simple loop / the probabilistic map.

> Will it necessarily be better? And if so, would it not be better for the source generator to precompute that?

Currently cases like `span.IndexOfAnyExcept(5 values)` will go to [`ProbabilisticMap.IndexOfAny`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/fb001c47d8fe6575c390fa7fc47b039917882841/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/ProbabilisticMap.cs#L103), which may use a for loop or spend a few extra cycles for the init cost of the ASCII bitmap/probabilistic map on every call.
`IndexOfAnyValues` would be faster in this case as we pay the init cost upfront.

The source generator could of course do as good/better of a job at the cost of increasing the amount of code it emits.

> Depends on how many specialized cases we wanted to implement

If we special-case 4 and 5 inputs with a concrete type that can be devirtualized and just delegate to the internal 4/5-overload versions, I'm fine removing the reliance on the 4/5-based IndexOfAny overload and just using the new one for those as well.

> when not on Mono

The Mono situation is temporary.  It resulted from a last minute revert due to lack of generic specialization in certain circumstances.  The same pattern is used by the new IndexOfAny vectorized changes.  I expect the issue to be fixed in Mono (it may already be) and the special-casing for Mono reverted.
If this is now potentially vectorized, should the `MaxUnrollSize` be lowered to 7?

Just because it's vectorized doesn't mean it's faster at 8.  There's the overhead of the method call and the other startup costs associated with the vectorization.  I'd be fine changing it if we can demonstrate with perf testing that doing so is a clear win.
